Free JEV calls, when available, use the operator’s key. You can connect your own TypeSafe or OpenRouter key instead; provider charges then apply. Both options go through Forma’s backend to the official provider. Exported sites never receive a key.
After a successful test, your API key is saved in this browser so you don’t have to enter it again. It is not saved in project files or exports. Select Remove key to delete it from this browser.
Projects stay in this browser profile and are visible to anyone using it. No account or cloud backup is provided. Export important work before clearing browser data.
Do I need to install anything?
No installation is needed for this hosted editor. Use the same browser profile to reopen projects, and download JSON backups for safekeeping.

Projects and uploaded images are saved in this browser profile, where anyone using the profile can open them. There is no cloud backup. Free JEV builds use the operator’s key. A personal key that passes the connection test is also saved in this browser profile and passes through Forma’s backend only for your connection tests and live builds. Select Remove key in the connection dialog to delete it.

Forma uses necessary cookies for the anonymous session and to verify requests, with no tracking or advertising cookies. Browser storage keeps your projects, preferences and, after a successful connection test, your personal API key. Free JEV calls use the operator’s key and are limited per public IP address. A design normally uses 2 provider calls. Free access allows 10 calls per public IP address each UTC day, when available. Testing your own key uses one billable call; builds using it are billed to you. Offline demo makes no provider calls.
